2 years ago I would have recommended this game to anyone who was hesitant to buy it. Today, I sincerely advise against such a purchase. The game is clearly abandoned. It had great potential, which was unfortunately wasted by the developer's incompetent management. The lack of any plan for its development and decisive decisions to reach a wider audience has caused the resignation of many dedicated players and made it more dead than ever.

Lets talk balance. 

Barrett and M79 were the meta in Soldat 1 and all skilled players used it. These weapons had a high skill ceiling AND a high skill floor. Now these weapons have been nerfed to oblivion. 

I know the developer wants to encourage players to try out other weapons, but other weapons are just not fun. There is not enough skill involved. You dont get the satisfaction when you manage to pull off a kill, nor do you get the certainty "If I don't make a mistake I am sure to win" that you get from Barrett and M79.

The server password protection feature doesn't work and someone who is presumably a friend of the developer invaded a private match. When I notified the soldat 2 community discord of this issue I was met with abuse and told this was normal. Great game, but off putting community.

This game is still early access. Development is slow, but stable. The developer (MM) is a real good guy. The community is worth investing time into: lots of down to earth, chill adults, who also like to compete. There are some minor in-game bugs, that make we want to headbutt the pope (in true Soldat players' eyes, MM is pretty much the pope), but the core gameplay is annoyingly good. It's very diverse. For competitive play, there's several dimensions of skill, each with infinite skill ceiling. If you start playing multiplayer now:
You can master movement (few hundreds of gameplay to be *average*)
You can master aim (few thousands of hours of gameplay to reach 40% accuracy in a competitive match)
You can master strategy (few thousands of hours of gameplay to *draw* a competitive match when you must)
You can master tactics (few hundreds of hours of gameplay get you a single double kill in a match)
You can master offense, defense, support.
You can master any combination of primary and secondary weapons to the point where others will want to ban your guns from the game, because you are that annoyingly good.
There's at least a thousand different armanent configurations with 20ish primaries and 5ish secondaries.
You can wield two grenades, a minigun, two desert eagles... Wearing nothing but white underpants and sunglasses. You can use jetpacks to headbutt people to death in an actual competitive game. Happens every day.
Game has active tournament scene with regular events on the horizon.
Core competitive community is 30-ish regular people. Friends. You can play competitive with them any day, pretty much any time. Discord is very active.
Wider competitive community is 100-ish respectful people. They appear out of thin air during tournaments.

For casual play, there's several dimensions of stupidity that you can explore. Tons of fun to be had. Readily available public servers, with good ping, running different combinations of maps, mods, and whatever the ♥♥♥♥ people can come up with. Some dude made a mod where everyone has pretty much infinite throwing knives. Knives bounce for 30 seconds with 100kph from walls. Deathmatch. 5 people. You need to avoid *all* knives for 5 minutes, while throwing back *infinite bouncing knives* to win. Everybody wants to win. I have not experienced that vibe anywhere else.

Soldat is a unique game. It is not meant for everyone. I personally use it as an outlet for my anger. Every other day I drink a beer, I sit down with Soldat, grab a chainsaw, and cut whoever the ♥♥♥♥ is on a random online server. I don't care if I win or die, because I respawn instantly. I cut up a fair amount of people, while ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and chatting as if I was in a pub. For some reason I'm accepted as a reasonably friendly player. That's who soldateers are: Open, friendly and welcoming adults, but you need to be on point. If you're being an ass to another community member, we will point you out. In extreme cases, players were banned for messing with other people's game.

For me it was well worth the 13 euros I paid. I keep coming back to it. When I have to speak to a certain colleague, I know that I'll be playing Soldat that evening.

I truly hope this game succeeds, and I'll try my best to contribute. The game and the developer deserves support. LAN parties deserve Soldat. Middle schools deserve Soldat in computer class. Therapy sessions deserve Soldat. Soldat is cheaper than any other drug I know.

The first Soldat is easily my most played game. I even learned programming and Photoshop just to make scripts and interfaces for S1, so it wouldn't be a stretch to say that a single game has influenced my career. So, after thousands of hours played, I feel experienced enough to be able to compare it to its successor.

[b]Soldat 2 is shaping up to be a worthy sequel.[/b] It's dynamic, the movement is just right, the new weapons introduce cool ways of eliminating each other, and the new maps look and feel great. Especially after the total rehaul update, the game embraced its arcade nature and has gotten visually appealing and clear at the same time. I just love how shooting the rocket launcher brings me back to Quake 2 times, where calculating the enemy's trajectory in your mind resulted in a satisfying kill. Guiding the RPG projectile also adds a new way of dealing with sneakier players, and the explosions push knives around for even more unexpected frags.

Thanks to the friendly community, we're getting more maps (there's a built-in map editor), external sites for tracking stats, and lots of cool ideas for improvements during early access. Its playerbase slowly grows, so seeing 6v6 matches on public servers is becoming a more common sight lately – but if pubs are not for you, you're more than welcome to join ranked 3v3 matches and get your posterior kicked.

Overall, I'm having lots of fun with Soldat 2, even during its early access. I'm confident that it's going to grow in the coming months, so I better go back to mastering the rocket launcher.
